item.title: RNN,LSTM,GRU
item.description:
Recurrent architectures process sequential data by maintaining an internal hidden state that persists information across time steps.

1. Standard Recurrent Neural Network (Vanilla RNN)

A standard RNN processes an input sequence x=(x1,x2,…,xT)\mathbf{x} = (\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, \dots, \mathbf{x}_T)x=(x1​,x2​,…,xT​) step-by-step. At each time step ttt, it updates its hidden state ht\mathbf{h}_tht​ based on the current input xt\mathbf{x}_txt​ and the previous hidden state ht−1\mathbf{h}_{t-1}ht−1​.

Mathematical Formulation

ht=tanh⁡(Whhht−1+Wxhxt+bh) \mathbf{h}_t = \tanh(\mathbf{W}_{hh} \mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{W}_{xh} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{b}_h) ht​=tanh(Whh​ht−1​+Wxh​xt​+bh​)y^t=σ(Whyht+by) \hat{\mathbf{y}}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_{hy} \mathbf{h}_t + \mathbf{b}_y) y^​t​=σ(Why​ht​+by​)
  • xt∈Rd\mathbf{x}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d}xt​∈Rd: Input vector at time step ttt.
  • ht∈Rh\mathbf{h}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{h}ht​∈Rh: Hidden state at time step ttt.
  • Whh∈Rh×h\mathbf{W}_{hh} \in \mathbb{R}^{h \times h}Whh​∈Rh×h, Wxh∈Rh×d\mathbf{W}_{xh} \in \mathbb{R}^{h \times d}Wxh​∈Rh×d, Why∈Rk×h\mathbf{W}_{hy} \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times h}Why​∈Rk×h: Weight matrices.
  • bh∈Rh\mathbf{b}_h \in \mathbb{R}^{h}bh​∈Rh, by∈Rk\mathbf{b}_y \in \mathbb{R}^{k}by​∈Rk: Bias vectors.
  • tanh⁡\tanhtanh: Hyperbolic tangent activation function, mapping values to (−1,1)(-1, 1)(−1,1).

Limitation: The Vanishing/Exploding Gradient Problem

When training via Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT), the gradient of the loss LT\mathcal{L}_TLT​ with respect to h1\mathbf{h}_1h1​ requires computing a chain of Jacobian matrices:

∂hT∂h1=∏k=2T∂hk∂hk−1=∏k=2Tdiag(1−hk2)WhhT \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}_T}{\partial \mathbf{h}_1} = \prod_{k=2}^T \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}_k}{\partial \mathbf{h}_{k-1}} = \prod_{k=2}^T \text{diag}(1 - \mathbf{h}_k^2) \mathbf{W}_{hh}^T ∂h1​∂hT​​=k=2∏T​∂hk−1​∂hk​​=k=2∏T​diag(1−hk2​)WhhT​

If the largest eigenvalue of Whh\mathbf{W}_{hh}Whh​ is less than 1, gradients decay exponentially toward zero as TTT grows, making it impossible to capture long-term dependencies.

2. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)

Introduced by Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997), LSTMs solve vanishing gradients by introducing a cell state (ct\mathbf{c}_tct​) that acts as an information highway, regulated by three multiplicative gating mechanisms.

Gates and Operations

  1. Forget Gate (ft\mathbf{f}_tft​): Determines what proportion of the old cell state to discard. ft=σ(Wf[ht−1,xt]+bf) \mathbf{f}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_f [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_f) ft​=σ(Wf​[ht−1​,xt​]+bf​)
  2. Input Gate (it\mathbf{i}_tit​) & Candidate Cell State (c~t\tilde{\mathbf{c}}_tc~t​): Determines what new information to store in the cell state. it=σ(Wi[ht−1,xt]+bi) \mathbf{i}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_i [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_i) it​=σ(Wi​[ht−1​,xt​]+bi​) c~t=tanh⁡(Wc[ht−1,xt]+bc) \tilde{\mathbf{c}}_t = \tanh(\mathbf{W}_c [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_c) c~t​=tanh(Wc​[ht−1​,xt​]+bc​)
  3. Cell State Update (ct\mathbf{c}_tct​): Combines retained past information and scaled new candidate information via linear additive operations: ct=ft⊙ct−1+it⊙c~t \mathbf{c}_t = \mathbf{f}_t \odot \mathbf{c}_{t-1} + \mathbf{i}_t \odot \tilde{\mathbf{c}}_t ct​=ft​⊙ct−1​+it​⊙c~t​
  4. Output Gate (ot\mathbf{o}_tot​) & Hidden State (ht\mathbf{h}_tht​): Controls what parts of the cell state make it to the output and next hidden state: ot=σ(Wo[ht−1,xt]+bo) \mathbf{o}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_o [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_o) ot​=σ(Wo​[ht−1​,xt​]+bo​) ht=ot⊙tanh⁡(ct) \mathbf{h}_t = \mathbf{o}_t \odot \tanh(\mathbf{c}_t) ht​=ot​⊙tanh(ct​)
  • σ(z)=11+e−z\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}σ(z)=1+e−z1​: Sigmoid function outputting values in (0,1)(0, 1)(0,1) to act as soft binary gates.
  • ⊙\odot⊙: Hadamard (element-wise) product.
  • [ht−1,xt]∈Rh+d[\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] \in \mathbb{R}^{h + d}[ht−1​,xt​]∈Rh+d: Concatenation of the previous hidden state and the current input.

Why LSTM Fixes Vanishing Gradients

The derivative of the cell state with respect to the previous cell state contains an additive component:

∂ct∂ct−1=ft+… \frac{\partial \mathbf{c}_t}{\partial \mathbf{c}_{t-1}} = \mathbf{f}_t + \dots ∂ct−1​∂ct​​=ft​+…

When the network learns to keep ft≈1\mathbf{f}_t \approx 1ft​≈1, the gradient flows backward across time steps without exponential decay.

3. Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)

Proposed by Cho et al. (2014), the GRU simplifies the LSTM by merging the cell state and hidden state into a single vector ht\mathbf{h}_tht​ and reducing the number of gates from three to two.

Gates and Operations

  1. Reset Gate (rt\mathbf{r}_trt​): Determines how much of the previous state ht−1\mathbf{h}_{t-1}ht−1​ to forget when computing the new candidate state. rt=σ(Wr[ht−1,xt]+br) \mathbf{r}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_r [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_r) rt​=σ(Wr​[ht−1​,xt​]+br​)
  2. Update Gate (zt\mathbf{z}_tzt​): Acts simultaneously as both the forget gate and input gate, regulating how much of the past state to keep versus how much of the candidate state to incorporate. zt=σ(Wz[ht−1,xt]+bz) \mathbf{z}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_z [\mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_z) zt​=σ(Wz​[ht−1​,xt​]+bz​)
  3. Candidate Hidden State (h~t\tilde{\mathbf{h}}_th~t​): Computes new candidate information, using rt\mathbf{r}_trt​ to selectively mask past context. h~t=tanh⁡(Wh[rt⊙ht−1,xt]+bh) \tilde{\mathbf{h}}_t = \tanh(\mathbf{W}_h [\mathbf{r}_t \odot \mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t] + \mathbf{b}_h) h~t​=tanh(Wh​[rt​⊙ht−1​,xt​]+bh​)
  4. Hidden State Update (ht\mathbf{h}_tht​): Linear interpolation between the previous hidden state and the candidate hidden state governed by zt\mathbf{z}_tzt​: ht=(1−zt)⊙ht−1+zt⊙h~t \mathbf{h}_t = (1 - \mathbf{z}_t) \odot \mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{z}_t \odot \tilde{\mathbf{h}}_t ht​=(1−zt​)⊙ht−1​+zt​⊙h~t​
